title: Oncall field diary — throttles, timeouts, and stream hiccups (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working runbook / oncall field diary for common API failure archetypes we keep seeing: client-facing timeouts, sudden 429 throttles, degraded streaming (lossy chunks / very long stalls), and sudden upticks in 5xx/error rates. The goal is operator-first: quick signal checks, low-cost mitigations, and safe escalation triggers.

Notes-to-self (high-level):
- Keep mitigation steps cheap and reversible. Prefer configuration toggles and routing rules before code changes.
- Capture metrics snapshots early (5m/1h) to aid postmortem.
- If multiple failure modes present (timeouts + 429s) treat the 429s as likely upstream rate-limiter or burst protection, not downstream service.

Quick triage checklist (first 5 minutes):
1) Confirm alert details and scope:
   - Which endpoint(s) are affected? (generation, chat, embeddings, streaming)
   - Is it global or region-specific? Check region tags in traces.
   - Confirm user-visible impact and SLO breaches.
2) Check high-level dashboards:
   - API gateway 95/99 latency, error rate by route.
   - Upstream model pool utilization (GPU/replica saturation).
   - Token-per-request distribution change (sudden spike in input or output length).
3) Pull logs and traces: last 10 minutes of samples for affected route.
   - Look for common signatures: slow backend RPCs, long queue times, repeated connection resets.

Common signatures and likely causes:
- Symptom: sudden spike in 429s for many customer keys
  Diagnosis: global throttling or quota bug, burst protection triggered (apparent load spike).
  Actions: verify rate-limiter config, check recent config rollouts.

- Symptom: incremental timeouts on generation endpoints, latency climbing gradually
  Diagnosis: queue/backpressure + model instance CPU/GPU saturation or kernel slowdown (e.g., longer sequences).
  Actions: check model-host metrics (GPU utilization, p95 inference time), prefix caching hit rates.

- Symptom: streaming responses stall mid-stream then resume or cut out
  Diagnosis: connection-level backpressure, HTTP/2 multiplex limits, proxy idle timeouts, or KV cache thrash causing long tail tokens.
  Actions: check proxy logs for reset/timeout, check worker logs for long GC or steal.

- Symptom: large batch of 5xx errors with similar stack traces
  Diagnosis: deployment bug, library upgrade, or memory error on specific binary.
  Actions: check recent deploys, correlate with CI/CD timeline, look for OOMs / segfaults.

Operator playbook (concrete steps):
A) For widespread 429s:
  1. Identify whether 429s are returned by our edge or by a downstream service (model infra, third-party). Inspect response headers (x-rate-limit, x-upstream).
  2. If edge-level throttle: temporarily increase per-route burst window (config flag: rate_limit.burst_override) for a short window (10m) while we stabilize.
  3. If caused by a commit to the rate limiter config, rollback that change immediately and monitor.
  4. Notify growth/partners if this affects quota-sensitive customers (email Slack #gcs-alerts).

B) For rising timeouts on generation endpoints:
  1. Expand the time window for traces (10m -> 1h) and capture a few slow traces.
  2. If model-host GPU utilization > 85% and queue length > threshold: trigger autoscale (if on Dedicated) or increase replica count for the affected model profile.
  3. If autoscale is failing or not available: reduce per-request concurrency by adjusting endpoint concurrency limit (endpoint.concurrency_max -> -20%) as a temporary throttle.
  4. Consider enabling degraded-mode fallback: route to a smaller/lower-latency model profile with reduced token budget. Documented config: routing.fallback_profile = "llama-latency-1b"

C) For degraded streaming:
  1. Check proxy (nginx/envoy) for connection resets or HTTP/2 flow-control logs.
  2. Adjust proxy keepalive and max-concurrent-streams for the immediate region. Typical safe change: max_concurrent_streams +50 for 15 minutes.
  3. If stalls coincide with client-side abrupt disconnects, check client SDK version in logs and coordinate with devx team to push a patched SDK.
  4. If worker-side long tail token generation: increase streaming chunk interval (server.stream_chunk_ms -> +50ms) to reduce tight loop scheduling.

D) For elevated 5xx/error rates concentrated in a deployment:
  1. Pinpoint the deployment via service tags and pod annotations. 2. Rollback suspicious revision(s) via release manager.
  2. If rollback unavailable: cordon affected instances and shift traffic with weighted routing to healthy instances.
  3. Collect core dumps / error logs (set TEMP_DUMP=1) and attach to incident ticket.

Safe escalation matrix:
- After 10 minutes and no mitigation progress -> page the on-call SRE lead (phone).
- If customer-impacting for >30 minutes or affecting enterprise customers -> page eng manager + solutions-eng + account manager.
- If rolling latency/availability correlated with infra degradation (disk/GPU failures) -> page infra-ops and cloud vendor (if applicable).

Run contexts and quick commands (examples):
- Grab 5 slow traces for route /v1/generate:
  curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/search?route=/v1/generate&latency>5000&limit=5" | jq '.'
- Check 1m queue length on model pool 'cascade-1':
  curl -s "https://infra.internal/metrics?pool=cascade-1&metric=queue_length&window=60s"

Mitigation guardrails (do not do without approval):
- Don’t disable global rate limiting entirely — only increase burst window or per-route window.
- Avoid long-term routing to lower-quality models without product sign-off (customer expectations).
- Do not change token billing configurations during an incident.

Post-incident checklist (short):
- Export snapshots: dashboards (5m/1h/24h), trace samples, edge logs.
- Identify root cause hypothesis and candidate engineering fix.
- Create a follow-up ticket with owners, timeline, and mitigations (link in linked_artifacts).
- Run a dry-run of proposed config change in staging for 48h monitoring.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we get a per-customer streaming connection gauge in the console? (helpful for diagnosing noisy clients)
- Need a safer automated fallback policy: prefer smaller model variant with quality checks. (Product + Research sync)
- Instrument HTTP/2 connection reset reasons into our telemetry (envoy metrics).

Recent incident notes (field captures):
- 2026-01-12 04:22 UTC: regional spawning of 429s in us-west-2; root cause: misconfigured burst window after a rate-limiter rollout. Mitigation: rolled back config; applied temporary +30% burst; closed after 24m.
- 2026-01-29 19:10 UTC: streaming stalls affecting ~3% of requests; correlated with client SDK v1.4.2 that changed keepalive behavior. Mitigation: blocked that SDK release; pushed note to devx; increased proxy keepalive for 2 hours.

Notes for postmortem writers:
- Include exact config hashes for any changes; record the API key(s) or tenant IDs impacted (redact as needed).
- Attach representative slow traces and the 429 header sets.

Appendix: quick heuristics for root cause mapping:
- 429 + uniform across keys -> throttler misconfiguration or global quota enforcement.
- 429 + narrow (single customer) -> abuse/noisy tenant; engage account team.
- Timeouts + model-host high GPU -> capacity -> scale or fallback.
- Streaming mid-stream cutoffs + proxy resets -> network/proxy limit or client behavior.

End-of-document TODOs (for this draft):
- Add exact playbook commands for autoscale APIs (who has perms?)
- Add example Terraform snippets for temporary burst_override config and how to revert
- Coordinate with devx to create a customer-facing status blurb template for these classes of incidents

-- Aisha (oncall notes)
